$comment: Policy for the ProxyPilot self-update MCP tools. `enabled: false` turns the run tool off without touching code (the two read-only tools keep working) — an operator who wants updates to be dashboard-only flips it here. run_proxypilot_update is confirm-gated like every other mutating verb, never takes --discard-local (the runner refuses it anyway), and refuses on its own when the host checkout has uncommitted changes, when a run is already live, when the host agent cannot be reached, or when no checkout was ever recorded. This JSON is the enforcement source of truth (routes/mcp.js loads it); the tool descriptions only summarize it.

check_proxypilot_update.note: GitHub latest release + latest main commit, the Mock2 standards manifest, and the host checkout facts. Cached for 10 minutes; force: true bypasses the cache.

get_proxypilot_update_status.note: The runner's state.json plus a bounded log tail. Answers before, during and after the container rebuild because the state lives on the host.

run_proxypilot_update.note: Writes one request for the root-owned runner (deploy/proxypilot-update.service). What runs is `update.sh --yes` with at most --rebuild — the same thing the dashboard's Update now button does.

explicitly_absent.discard_local: Throwing away the operator's uncommitted changes on the host is a hands-on decision: `update.sh --yes --discard-local` at a shell, never over MCP.
explicitly_absent.auto_update: No tool schedules or repeats updates; every run is one explicit confirm: true call.
